title: GPT-6-Astra solves 49 of 50 physics research problems at $2.40 apiece
key_facts: 35 researchers from institutions including ICTS, Harvard, KU Leuven and Google DeepMind released TheoPhysEval, a benchmark of 50 unpublished theoretical physics research problems with verifiable answers.
OpenAI's GPT-6-Astra in the Codex environment solved 49 of 50 (98 percent) with no human hints, at under $3 per problem and just under $116 for the whole benchmark.
Anthropic's Opus 5.5 in Claude Code scored 92 percent, Gemini 3.8 Flash 68 percent, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 54 percent and GLM 5.3 42 percent.
Without web search, Astra and Opus each scored 92 percent, which the authors read as a sign models have memorized much of the theoretical physics literature.
The problems are 'turn-the-crank' calculations; the authors say agents lack the 'taste' to choose good problems and that this is not a forecast.
The authors warn that rising compute needs could make a group's budget matter more even in theoretical physics, raising access and equal-opportunity questions.
quote_evidence: GPT-6-Astra, running in OpenAI's Codex coding environment, came out on top.
It found the right answer for 49 of 50 problems, or 98 percent, at an average cost of under $3 per problem and just under $116 for the whole benchmark.
Agents don't seem to have this "taste" yet.
why_it_matters_hint: Top AI agents now match specialists on concrete physics calculations, which may change how early-career researchers are trained and who can afford research.
notes: Full text read. Benchmark is the authors' own; no independent review reported.
